reason: Recounts specification coverage for readcon-core 0.24.0 without rewriting the previous measurement.

clauses.reason: A writer rule against an extra blank line between frames. A reader still finds the next frame; no corpus file has that blank as its only fault.
A MAY that leaves lines 5 and 6 empty. The reader accepts an empty line and a filled one, and the clause names no rejection.

A SHOULD NOT that turns on the consumer a file is written for. No writer of the library, in Rust, Python or the C ABI, takes a consumer or a target version: the arguments name the destination, the frames, the float format or precision, compression, canonical order and the MPI settings, so no writer call states the clause.
Coordinate blocks follow the header order. The parser reads them in that order; no corpus file is only a reordered block.
A spec 2 writer must not emit 1 for all-fixed. The writer emits 7, and a legacy 1 stays all-fixed for a reader of spec 1.
A spec 2 writer emits 7 for an atom fixed on x, y and z. That is the same writer path as CON-mask.6.
A reader must not assume an id starts at 0 or 1. The parser accepts any integer id, and no probe is named with this clause.
A consumer that returns atoms in pre-grouping order uses CON-id.5. The library returns file order, so this consumer rule has no call.
A writer must not put a blank line between the component blocks of a section. No corpus file is only that blank.
The per-atom energy section name is energies. The parser looks up that name.
atom_energies is not a section name. An unknown name is skipped with the unknown-section rule.
A rule for revising the specification: adding a reserved section name raises con_spec_minor. It states nothing a reader or a writer does.
A rule for revising the specification: adding a reserved section name needs no new major. It states nothing a reader or a writer does.

A SHOULD on the values a producer stores. CON-section.19 forbids a reader to reject a frame whose energy differs from the sum of its energies rows, and scripts/clause_coverage.py shows that no corpus file, probe or named test cites that clause.
A reader must not reject a frame whose energy differs from the sum of its energies rows. scripts/clause_coverage.py shows that no corpus file, probe or named test cites that clause.
validate true must not relax a check that already applies. The flag only adds checks.
bonds must not appear in sections. The named bonds probes are CON-bonds.2, a malformed bonds entry.
scripts/indep_reader.py rejects a malformed bonds entry. The scan reads the corpus, the referee probes and the library tests, not that reader.
A consumer may apply a velocity time-unit override when a file breaks CON-units.8 through CON-units.10. No library call takes that override.
The C ABI absent-value NaN is not a file token. The writer prints a finite decimal and refuses a non-finite coordinate.
A writer may split one frame across gzip members and store an RCZ1 index. src/iterators.rs checks that the index bytes are present; the test name does not spell this clause.
A writer may split one frame across zstd frames with the same RCZ1 index. A one-frame zstd file has no index, and that is the file the corpus reads.
An integer token is ASCII digits with no sign and no decimal point. The finite-number parser rejects the other spellings, and the tests name the function rather than this clause.
